# 196 · A route renamed in the refactor, left unresolved with a question for each observation it carried

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **⚠ Unverifiable** | compatibility | medium | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`QuotesController#quote`](../../examples/apps/shop/src/main/java/shop/QuotesController.java) | [B9: Regression verification](../../lib/README.md) |

> The value-object refactor of 190, with `POST /quotes` renamed to `POST /quote`. Its observations are a consumer's: no proof about the new route can stand in for the old one without a person saying the rename is intended. The tool leaves the old route unresolved, counts its four observations as removed and the new route's as new, and asks a person about each.

Tags: [payments](../README.md#tag-payments), [spring-boot](../README.md#tag-spring-boot), [request-binding](../README.md#tag-request-binding), [joint-run](../README.md#tag-joint-run), [effect-trace](../README.md#tag-effect-trace), [own-checker](../README.md#tag-own-checker)

## The change

`Quote`'s amount, a `long` of cents, becomes a value object, `Money`, so `Quote(long cents, int quantity)` is now `Quote(Money amount, int quantity)`; `Pricing.total` reads `q.amount.cents()` where it read `q.cents`; the pure helper `Pricing.discount` (a tenth off ten items or more) is rewritten as an early return; and the route `POST /quotes` makes the quote with `new Money(cents)`. Nothing is meant to change: not the total, not the event the route sends, not what `Pricing.withQuantity` hands back. In this version the route's path is also `/quote`.

**Before** ([`QuotesController.java`](../../examples/apps/shop/src/main/java/shop/QuotesController.java), line 14):

```java
        this.kafka = kafka;
    }

    @PostMapping("/quotes")
    public long quote(@RequestParam long cents, @RequestParam int quantity) {
        long total = Pricing.total(new Quote(cents, quantity));
        if (total > 0) kafka.send("quotes", new QuoteEvent(total, quantity));
        return total;
    }
    // ...
    /** The case this loop leaves unresolved: a string response, built by string concatenation. */
    @PostMapping("/quotes/text")
    public String quoteText(@RequestParam long cents, @RequestParam int quantity) {
        return "total " + Pricing.total(new Quote(cents, quantity));
    }
}
```

**After:**

```java
        this.kafka = kafka;
    }

    @PostMapping("/quote")
    public long quote(@RequestParam long cents, @RequestParam int quantity) {
        long total = Pricing.total(new Quote(new Money(cents), quantity));
        if (total > 0) kafka.send("quotes", new QuoteEvent(total, quantity));
        return total;
    }
    // ...
    /** The case this loop leaves unresolved: a string response, built by string concatenation. */
    @PostMapping("/quotes/text")
    public String quoteText(@RequestParam long cents, @RequestParam int quantity) {
        return "total " + Pricing.total(new Quote(new Money(cents), quantity));
    }
}
```

## What the verifier found

The run left `shop.QuotesController#quote` without a verdict:

- `POST /quotes has no counterpart in examples/apps/shop/build/main: removed, renamed, or not told apart from another`

Every part the run checked, nothing written by hand (the entry points under their observation specs, each kernel pair under the correspondence alignment proposed), and what the rerun on the same proof cache took from the first run:

| Part | Kind | Verdict | On the rerun | Why not verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /quotes` | entry point | unresolved | not a proof | `POST /quotes has no counterpart in examples/apps/shop/build/main: removed, renamed, or not told apart from another` |
| `POST /quotes/text` | entry point | unresolved | not a proof | `what the analysis can't see stays unresolved: the old build: a dynamic call site the walk doesn't follow: StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants in QuotesController.quoteText(long, int) (string concatenation: the string's value isn't modeled); the new build: a dynamic call site the walk doesn't follow: StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants in QuotesController.quoteText(long, int) (string concatenation: the string's value isn't modeled)` |
| `shop.Pricing#discount` | kernel | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `shop.Pricing#total` | kernel | verified | an exact hit; `Pricing.discount` proved on its own and taken as one function |  |
| `shop.Pricing#withQuantity` | kernel | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `shop.Money#cents (was shop.Quote#cents)` | kernel | unresolved | not a proof | `class not found in the previous version: shop.Money` |
| `shop.Quote#quantity` | kernel | unresolved | not a proof | `the receiver is made differently in the two versions: this: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(cents: long, quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts before, this: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(amount: Money(cents: long), quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts now; a receiver of another construction or other fields is not supported yet` |

Obligations, one per observation of an old entry point: 4 new, 3 preserved, 4 removed, 1 unresolved. Decisions a person made, by category: approved exclusion 0, domain restriction 0, environment assumption 0, mapping 0, observation change 0.

Questions left for a person (the result stays unresolved until one answers):

- `POST /quotes` (observation change): POST /quotes is gone from the new build: approve its result as removed, or it stays unresolved
- `POST /quotes` (observation change): POST /quotes is gone from the new build: approve its exception as removed, or it stays unresolved
- `POST /quotes` (observation change): POST /quotes is gone from the new build: approve its status as removed, or it stays unresolved
- `POST /quotes` (observation change): POST /quotes is gone from the new build: approve its effect:org/springframework/kafka/core/KafkaTemplate#send(Ljava/lang/String;Ljava/lang/Object;)Ljava/lang/Object; as removed, or it stays unresolved

What the verdicts rest on that nobody decided (assumed, not approved):

- KafkaTemplate.send is a recording stub in both builds: a recorded attempt is the call attempted, with its payload snapshotted at the call, not a delivery or a commit
- every modeled call returns normally, the environment model's only outcome: a failure of a store, broker or client is outside the claim
- QuotesController is made by its constructor with every dependency null and every other argument zero, in both builds: its dependencies are reached only through the modeled calls, and configuration it would be given is the type's default
- a payload string is snapshotted as the literal it is, among those of either build; any other string leaves the result unresolved
- at most 4 attempts are recorded, exactly in order; one more leaves the result unresolved

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

No: every existing unit test passes (`java -ea shop.Tests`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

A rename of a route breaks every client of the old path, and a tool that matched routes by their handler, or reused the old route's proof for the new one, would report the change as preserved.

## Why the verdict is right

Entry points are matched by their id, the method and path, as `observations --against` matches them, so `POST /quotes` has no counterpart and is unresolved, never proved against `POST /quote`. Its result, exception, status and event are each an obligation counted as removed, and each is a question for a person: approve it as removed, or it stays unresolved. No proof is looked up for it, so no cached result of the old route is reused.

## What to do

Keep the old path, or approve the rename as an intended change to what the route's consumers observe.

## Notes

- Checked by `jvmcontract compare`, which build.py runs as the B9 check of the shop app (`run_tool_compare`): the unpatched build against the patched one, twice under one fresh proof cache, the verdict read from the rerun and the page's output from the first run. The verdict is the subject's; the page lists every other part the run checked.
- The joint example of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md`'s Phase 5, made an example: the app's sources are the fixture's `before` build (`lib/tests/fixtures/foundations/`), and the patch turns them into its `after` build with the route-change defect (`defects/route-change/`) overlaid. `lib/tests/compare.rs` holds `jvmcontract compare` to the same builds inline; this is the same run by build.py, with the app's tests run too.
- Nothing in the run is written by hand. The entry points' external inputs (`cents`, `quantity`) are anchored by their observation specs, so no mapping is involved at the boundary. The kernel's relation between the old and new quotes (`old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents`, `old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity`) is alignment's proposal, inferred from how the two constructors route their parameters into the fields; it stays *proposed*, its evidence the proof under its claim key, and since nothing external anchors a kernel method's inputs, a proved relation there is reported as proved and not as the intended one.
- What stays unresolved in every example of the set, by name: `POST /quotes/text` (its string concatenation isn't modeled), `Quote#cents` moved to `Money#cents` (a method of a class the old build doesn't have) and the instance method `Quote#quantity` (the regression check takes static methods, or a record's over its primitive components).
- Run inline on 2026-11-07 (JDK 25.0.5), `jvmcontract compare` on the app compiled unpatched and patched, as build.py compiles it, and on the fixture's builds, with the same verdicts (the times are the fixture's): `POST /quotes` unresolved (no counterpart), 4 obligations removed and 4 new, 4 questions of the category observation change, no decision made; the kernel's `total`, `withQuantity` and `discount` verified. 0.3 s cold, 0.1 s warm.
- The app's tests pass on this version: they call the handler, not the path.
